library.description: RPC host with transport and feature plugins.

blocks.text: 用一个 `createRpcHost` 入口，把业务函数接到进程、线程、浏览器或协作任务。每个 host 安装一个传输 plugin，按需叠加 feature。
English · 使用指南

items: 调用与资源归属放在一起。 host 负责调用、目录和在途任务；传输 plugin 保留真实进程、Worker、监听器或借用资源的释放责任。
双向请求与流共用连接。 双方都可以 `provide`，用 `request` 等待结果、`notify` 等待物理发送、`stream` 逐项消费。
多对端行为明确。 不指定目标就是广播；指定直连目标用 `send` 或 `dispatch`，每个目标的失败独立保留。
功能按需安装。 期限、认证、重试、分片和类型生成使用公开 feature，不需要组装底层调用对象。

blocks.text: 安装 host、协议包和本例的协程传输：

blocks.code: pnpm add @migaia/rpc-host @migaia/rpc-contract @migaia/rpc-plugin-coroutines

blocks.text: 下面在同一事件循环建立两个真实 host。任务接收的 `connect` 是本代专属句柄；父端关闭后，任务沿原取消信号退出。
输出 `42`。需要独立进程或线程时，换用下表中的传输；业务 `provide` 和调用接口不变。

为现有调用链贡献配置或观察能力；同一 feature 定义每个 host 至多一次

blocks.text: `self` 可指定 `{ name, instanceId }`；省略时生成独立身份。名称用于直连选择，`instanceId` 区分实际实例。同名新连接会探测旧会话：旧会话仍响应则拒绝，已失效才接纳新会话。

blocks.text: 普通 host 的无目标调用：0 个目标返回 `{ fulfilled: {}, rejected: {} }`；1 个目标返回该标量，失败直接拒绝；多个目标返回按目标身份索引的 `fulfilled` / `rejected`。流集合中的每个迭代器独立取消。安装 pool 后只公开一个逻辑目标 `pool`，每次只调度一个成员并返回标量。
`send('b', 'c.render', payload)` 先到直连 b；b 必须确认 c 是自己当前存活的直连，再读取 c 当前目录并转发。a 不能直接指定未与自己连接的 c。也可在 b 使用 `provide({ render: b.peers.c.render })` 显式发布持有的能力；该能力不会悄悄改指重连后的新代。

rows: 子进程、本机服务、JSON-RPC 字节服务
同一事件循环的协作任务

blocks.text: 公用功能有两种等价的按需导入写法：

两种写法选一种安装；不能把同一 feature 的两个配置同时装进一个 host。`typegenFeature({ out: { write(fileName, text) { console.log(fileName, text) } } })` 读取已接受目录及方法 schema，应用负责实际文件 I/O。认证配置沿 `authFeature(config)` 的真实签名；不要把一项能力标签当作授权。
传输的 `connect: { timeoutMs }` 约束握手准备；业务调用的 `timeoutMs`、host 的 `defaultTimeoutMs` 和 timeout feature 是另一层。单次调用优先于 host 设置，host 设置优先于 feature 默认。`signal` 支持协作取消；到期或断开不能证明业务未执行，非幂等操作应先对账再决定重试。

错误按功能域区分：调用与 host 准入为 `rpc.endpoint`，远端托管调用为 `rpc.remote`，实际载体使用自己的 `rpc.transport.*`。按 `source` 与 `code` 判断，保留 `cause` / `errors` 和原生错误类型，不依赖消息文本。缺失/重复传输、无 SDK 身份、重复 feature/assembler、响应中的同名对端均在对应准入边界拒绝。
传输和 feature 是真实 plugin-host 定义，也可交给普通 `PluginHost.use(...)`；它的原安装、替换和清理 owner 保持负责。自定义传输作者使用 `@migaia/rpc-host/plugin` 的冷部署及作用域工具；应用从 `createRpcHost` 开始，不需要底层工厂或私有文件。
更多调用、取消与迁移说明见使用指南。
README · English
一个 `createRpcHost` 配置一个传输 plugin，再按需安装 feature。以下场景使用真实公开入口；传输准备、调用目录和原生清理由现有 owner 分别负责。

sections.id: 建立可完整关闭的双向连接
sections.heading: 建立可完整关闭的双向连接

blocks.text: 下面的完整示例只需要 host、contract 与 coroutines 三个包。父端安装 timeout feature；子端从本代 task 的 connect 句柄建立自己的 host。该节断言业务结果并输出 42，finally 关闭双方。
完整可运行示例放在后文“从旧包迁移”，同时演示父子 host、timeout feature 与 finally 清理。
协程用于同一事件循环，不是 Worker 隔离。换成 processPlugin 或 threadPlugin 时，业务 provide 与调用接口保持一致。每个 host 只有一个实际调用端点，多会话也不额外创建端点。

sections.id: 提供普通方法-生成器和协作取消
sections.heading: 提供普通方法、生成器和协作取消

blocks.text: provide 是嵌套函数对象；函数返回值成为结果，抛出的原错误走既有错误传输。相同方法名再次登记会拒绝，原登记不会被替换。
调用方通过 options.signal 取消；处理方读取自己的 context.signal。取消只终止对应调用，不是自动杀进程或回滚已执行副作用。示例 wait 专门等取消，真实工作应在自己的 finally 中释放资源。

sections.id: 明确选择目标与消费流
sections.heading: 明确选择目标与消费流

blocks.text: 声明可以是单个能力，或以直连名称映射的能力集合。下面的 helper 接受已连接的 host，保留目标与方法之间的类型关系：
无目标 request/notify/group/outcome 的普通 host 规则：0 个目标得到空 fulfilled/rejected；1 个目标返回标量、失败直接拒绝；多个目标按目标身份保留 fulfilled/rejected。stream 对多目标返回独立迭代器集合，单个 return/取消不影响其他迭代器。pool 是一个逻辑目标，因此总是只选一个成员执行。

sections.id: 通知-分组与结果不确定性
sections.heading: 通知、分组与结果不确定性

blocks.text: notify 的 Promise 表示物理发送完成，不表示业务处理完成。dispatch 同步返回 void，失败交给原报告通道。group 的步骤由每个选中目标处理，没有跨目标事务。outcome(key) 查询原幂等结果存储；连接恢复不能证明未确认业务没有执行。
调用 timeoutMs 优先于 host.defaultTimeoutMs，再优先于 timeoutFeature 默认；传输 connect.timeoutMs 独立约束握手。两种 feature 导入同一模块级定义，选一种安装，不在同一 host 重复安装：

blocks.code:
import timeoutFeature from '@migaia/rpc-host/features/timeout'

export const deadline = timeoutFeature({ ms: 1500 })

sections.heading: 发布转发能力与自动名称空间

blocks.text: b 先连接 c，再发布下面的能力，之后让调用方取得对应目录：
持有的函数绑定 c 原来的连接代次，退出后拒绝，不自动指向新实例。另一种是 a 调用 send('b', 'c.render', value)：b 先查 c 是当前存活直连，再查 c 当前目录。断开/重连期间以 TARGET_UNKNOWN 拒绝；未知方法保持原未知方法码。环路与第四次转发在进入业务前拒绝。名称无法表达为方法段时仍可直连调用或显式 provide 别名，不扩大方法语法。

blocks.text: 下面是使用新入口的完整替代示例。父端、子端和 timeout feature 都实际运行，并在 finally 关闭。
同一 host 只能安装一个传输、一个成员 assembler，同一 feature 定义至多一次。不能 spread/copy 定义后当成已注册 plugin；必须保留工厂实际返回对象。connect 参数描述安装时的连接准备，不是重复安装或热替换指令。
按 source/code 判断：rpc.endpoint 为 host/调用，rpc.remote 为托管远端结果，rpc.transport.* 为实际载体。保留原生类型、stack、cause 和 errors；不要匹配消息或把未知结果统一当成可重试。close/asyncDispose 沿相同原关闭 Promise；只关闭所拥有资源，借用原生载体仍由应用关闭。
普通 PluginHost 直接 use 这些真实定义，保留原替换与反向清理顺序。自定义来源作者使用 @migaia/rpc-host/plugin 的冷 raw deployment 与作用域能力，不能把完整旧调用对象冒充 source。进程、线程、浏览器、协程、池和观察器的各自指南说明原生归属。
Connect application functions across processes, threads, browsers, or cooperative tasks through `createRpcHost`. Install one transport plugin per host and add features as needed.
中文 · Usage guide

items: Calls and resource ownership stay connected. The host owns calls, directories, and pending work; the transport preserves native process, Worker, listener, and borrowed-resource ownership.
One connection supports both directions and streams. Both sides can `provide`; `request` waits for a result, `notify` for physical sending, and `stream` yields items.
Multiple targets have explicit results. Calls without a target broadcast. `send` and `dispatch` select a direct target, retaining each target's own failure.
Features configure the existing path. Add deadlines, authentication, retry, chunking, or type generation without assembling lower-level call objects.

blocks.text: Install the host, protocol module, and the coroutine transport used below:

blocks.code: pnpm add @migaia/rpc-host @migaia/rpc-contract @migaia/rpc-plugin-coroutines

blocks.text: This creates two real hosts in one event loop. The task's `connect` handle belongs to this generation; closing the parent cancels the task through its original signal.
It prints `42`. Choose another transport below for a separate process or thread; `provide` and the call interface stay the same.

rows: Local identity, providers, calls, and closure; one host constructs one call endpoint
Prepares the actual source; exactly one per host
Contributes configuration or observation to existing owners; each definition appears at most once per host
Ordinary functions or generators; return values become results and exceptions retain their error chain
Current direct capabilities; held functions remain bound to their original connection generation

blocks.text: Set `self` to `{ name, instanceId }`, or let the host generate an independent identity. Names select direct peers; instance IDs distinguish actual instances. A new connection with the same name probes the old session: a responsive old session rejects it, while a failed old session can be retired and replaced.

rows: Business results from current direct targets
Physical send completion, without business acknowledgement; `options.targetId` can select one direct target
One iterator or independent iterators indexed by target
A group of `{ method, payload }` steps per target, without a cross-target transaction
Retained logical outcomes on current targets
A scalar result from one current direct target
Single-target send with failure reporting; returns `void` synchronously
Adds local methods; duplicate names reject instead of replacing providers
Reads identity, directory, and state; observes existing lifecycle events
Releases the host; repeated calls share one Promise

blocks.text: For an ordinary host, an untargeted call returns `{ fulfilled: {}, rejected: {} }` with zero targets, a scalar with one target (rejecting on its failure), and `fulfilled` / `rejected` maps indexed by target identity with multiple targets. Stream iterators cancel independently. A pool exposes only `pool`: every operation selects one member and returns a scalar.

`send('b', 'c.render', payload)` reaches direct peer b first. b must verify that c is its current live direct peer before looking up c's current method directory and forwarding. a cannot directly select c without a connection. b can also explicitly publish a held capability through `provide({ render: b.peers.c.render })`; that function does not silently retarget a later generation.

rows: Child processes, local services, JSON-RPC byte services
Window, browser Workers, broadcast, ServiceWorker, RTC, WebTransport
Cooperative tasks in one event loop

blocks.text: Shared features support equivalent aggregate and individual imports:

Choose one spelling per installation, rather than installing two instances of the same definition. `typegenFeature({ out: { write(fileName, text) { console.log(fileName, text) } } })` reads accepted directories and method schemas; the application owns file I/O. Pass the actual authentication configuration to `authFeature(config)`; capability labels alone do not authorize calls.

Transport `connect: { timeoutMs }` bounds handshake preparation. Business-call `timeoutMs`, host `defaultTimeoutMs`, and timeout features are separate. A call override wins over host configuration, which wins over the feature default. `signal` supports cooperative cancellation. Expiry or disconnection does not prove that business code never executed; reconcile a non-idempotent result before retrying.

Error sources are functional domains: `rpc.endpoint` for calls and host admission, `rpc.remote` for managed remote calls, and `rpc.transport.*` for native carriers. Branch on `source` and `code`; retain native types, `cause`, and `errors` rather than matching messages. Missing/duplicate transports, unregistered definitions, duplicate feature/assembler definitions, and responsive same-name peers reject at their admission boundaries.

Transport and feature objects are genuine plugin-host definitions and also work with ordinary `PluginHost.use(...)`, retaining its existing installation, replacement, and cleanup owners. Transport authors use cold deployment and scope tools from `@migaia/rpc-host/plugin`. Applications start with `createRpcHost` and need no private files or lower-level factories.
See the usage guide for calls, cancellation, and migration.
README · 中文

Configure one transport plugin with `createRpcHost`, then install features as needed. These scenarios use real public entries; existing owners retain transport preparation, directories, and native cleanup.

sections.heading: Open and completely close a bidirectional connection

blocks.text: This complete example needs host, contract, and coroutines. The parent installs a timeout feature; the child creates its host from the generation-local connect handle. It asserts the business result, prints 42, and closes both sides through finally.
The complete runnable example appears under “Migrating from old module”, covering parent/child hosts, the timeout feature, and finally cleanup.

Coroutines share the event loop rather than Worker isolation. With processPlugin or threadPlugin, business providers and calls stay the same. Each host has one actual call endpoint, including a host with multiple sessions.

sections.heading: Provide functions, generators, and cooperative cancellation

blocks.text: provide is a nested function object. Return values become results and thrown errors use the existing error boundary. Registering a duplicate method rejects without replacing the original.

Callers cancel through options.signal; providers receive their own context.signal. Cancellation affects that call rather than killing a process or rolling back side effects. The wait example deliberately awaits cancellation; real work releases its own resources in finally.

sections.heading: Select a target and consume streams

blocks.text: A declaration can describe one capability or map direct names to capabilities. This helper accepts an already connected host and preserves the relationship between target and method:

An ordinary untargeted request/notify/group/outcome returns empty fulfilled/rejected maps with zero targets, a scalar with one target (rejecting on failure), and per-target fulfilled/rejected maps with multiple targets. Multi-target stream returns independent iterators; one return/cancellation does not cancel others. A pool is one logical target and selects one member per operation.

A notify Promise means physical sending completed, not that business work acknowledged it. dispatch returns void synchronously and reports failures. Each selected target owns its group; there is no cross-target transaction. outcome(key) reads the existing retained idempotency result. Reconnection does not prove that uncertain work never executed.

Call timeoutMs overrides host.defaultTimeoutMs, which overrides the timeoutFeature default. Transport connect.timeoutMs independently bounds handshake preparation. Aggregate and individual feature imports identify the same definition; install one spelling:

blocks.code:
import timeoutFeature from '@migaia/rpc-host/features/timeout'

export const deadline = timeoutFeature({ ms: 1500 })

sections.heading: Publish forwarding capabilities and automatic namespaces

blocks.text: Let b connect to c, publish this capability, then let callers obtain the resulting directory:

A held function stays bound to c's original generation and rejects after retirement. It does not retarget a successor. Alternatively, a calls send('b', 'c.render', value): b first verifies c is a current live direct peer, then reads c's current directory. Disconnected/reconnecting targets reject with TARGET_UNKNOWN; missing methods retain the existing method error. Loops and a fourth forwarding hop reject before business execution. Names that cannot form a method segment remain usable through direct selection or explicit provide aliases, without changing method grammar.

Install declarations in plugins. write is application-owned output; this example displays filename and text, while the application chooses actual file I/O. Generation follows accepted directories regardless of peer language. Method input/output/yield schemas come from the real contract description; a new generation writes only after acceptance. Uninstall stops further writes, and output failures reach host.report.

Rename module first: rpc-core→rpc-host, rpc-process→rpc-plugin-process, rpc-threads→rpc-plugin-thread, rpc-browser→rpc-plugin-browser, rpc-pool→rpc-plugin-pool, rpc-devtools→rpc-plugin-devtools. Coroutines live in rpc-plugin-coroutines. Old names below identify migrations rather than compatibility entries.

Install supported public features on the host; no preset or root graph
Host owns the one call endpoint; authors supply raw deployment through `/plugin`
Host plus transport; original native supervision owns generations
Host + transport + provide, or native plugin-host installation
Host plus one of the seven browser carrier plugins
`processPlugin` / `threadPlugin` installed on host or ordinary PluginHost
`coroutinePlugin` from its own module; child receives opaque connect handle
Transport + `poolPlugin`; logical target pool, one scalar execution
`devtoolsPlugin().collector`; install that same definition for observation

blocks.text: This complete replacement uses only new public entries. It runs the parent, child, and timeout feature, then closes them in finally.

Each host accepts one transport and one member assembler, with each feature definition appearing at most once. Keep the factory's actual registered object; copying/spreading it does not preserve registration authority. connect options configure preparation at installation, not repeated installation or hot replacement.

Branch on source/code: rpc.endpoint owns host/call errors, rpc.remote managed uncertainty, and rpc.transport.* native carriers. Keep native types, stack, cause, and errors. Do not match messages or assume unknown results are safely retryable. close/asyncDispose share the original close Promise and release owned resources; applications retain borrowed native ownership.

Ordinary PluginHost installs the same genuine definitions, retaining original replacement and reverse cleanup. Source authors use cold raw deployments and scope capabilities from @migaia/rpc-host/plugin, never a complete legacy call object as a source. Individual transport, pool, and observation guides explain their native ownership.

symbols.purpose: Installs original per-frame protection, actual physical-session binding and replay checks; encryption runs before signing, verification before decryption.
symbols.core:
encrypt: Outbound sync/async encryption runs after the endpoint wraps its encoded value with replay metadata and before signing. Throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with its cause.
encrypt.value: Replay-bound authentication envelope produced by the endpoint, including its encoded payload; not the bare application payload.
encrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Encrypted value or its Promise, passed unchanged into sign.
Leave encrypt and decrypt out together when messages need signatures but not encryption. In that case, sign receives the unencrypted authentication envelope: the message data together with the information used to detect replay. Omitting encryption does not remove signing or verification.
Configure `encrypt` with `decrypt` for confidentiality and `sign` with `verify` for integrity; `encodedType` names the actual protected representation.
decrypt: Inbound sync/async decryption runs on the value recovered by verify. The endpoint then validates the recovered authentication envelope and replay binding.
decrypt.value: Verified protected value returned by verify.
decrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Recovered replay-bound authentication envelope or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with the original cause.
Omit decrypt only when encrypt is also omitted. After verify checks the signature and recovers the inner value, the endpoint directly checks that value as the authentication envelope, including its replay information. It does not try to decrypt the value.
sign: Outbound sync/async signing runs after optional encryption and returns the complete protected frame representation. Signing and verification are required even without encryption.
sign.value: Encrypted value when encrypt exists, otherwise the replay-bound authentication envelope.
sign.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Signed representation or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Keep the declared encodedType output domain.
There is no default signing function. Provide sign together with verify whenever authentication is enabled. This remains required when encrypt and decrypt are configured: encryption alone is insufficient, and omitting sign rejects the configuration.
verify: Inbound sync/async verification receives the protected frame and must recover its authenticated inner value; returning a boolean is not a verification verdict protocol.
verify.value: Protected value received at the authentication pipeline edge.
verify.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Authenticated inner value or its Promise, passed to decrypt when configured; reject or throw on invalid signatures. Local reporting retains the original verification failure, which may be sensitive; the peer receives a sanitized summary. Other returned values still undergo envelope/replay validation.

encodedType: Declared protected-output domain must match the next physical pipeline edge. Encrypt/decrypt and sign/verify are complete pairs, at least signing is required, and encryption additionally requires signing.

symbols.signature: export type IRpcIdempotencyClaim = Readonly<{ /** * Claimed owns execution; pending waits for the original owner; done replays retention; full * refuses admission. */ status: 'claimed'; /** Settle this exact claim once with its outcome and settlement-relative monotonic time. */ settle: (outcome: IRpcIdempotencyOutcome, now: number) => void; /** Release an unsettled claim and resolve its waiting observers with undefined. */ release: () => void; }> | Readonly<{ /** * Claimed owns execution; pending waits for the original owner; done replays retention; full * refuses admission. */ status: 'pending'; /** * Original completed outcome or pending observation; unavailable means the body was not * retained. */ outcome: Promise<IRpcIdempotencyOutcome | 'unavailable' | undefined>; }> | Readonly<{ status: 'done'; outcome: IRpcIdempotencyOutcome | 'unavailable'; }> | Readonly<{ status: 'full'; }>;
symbols.purpose: One store claim owns execution, waits on original work, replays retained outcome, or refuses capacity; each status has a distinct available surface.
symbols.core:
status: Discriminates claimed, pending, done and full branches; narrow before using branch-specific methods.
This exact claim owns the first business execution.
Original business is still running; await its existing outcome.
Original business already settled; replay or report unavailable body.
No execution reservation was admitted at the current quota.
settle: On a claimed branch, settles once with the original portable business outcome and starts retention at the supplied time.
settle.outcome: Actual IRpcIdempotencyOutcome returned by the original business execution.

symbols.purpose: Stable semantic failure codes owned by the runtime-neutral Core execution layer. The stable values below select actual contract behavior; declarations alone grant no capability.
symbols.core:
providerGenerationMismatch: PROVIDER_GENERATION_MISMATCH: accepted caller/provider generation no longer matches the task; select the actual binding again.
providerGenerationRetired: PROVIDER_GENERATION_RETIRED: an admitted forwarded execution retired with its exact generation; never replay it.
forwardLoop: FORWARD_LOOP: signed route revisits this or the selected next Host; choose another route.
forwardHopLimit: FORWARD_HOP_LIMIT: three forwarding nodes were already visited; use a direct channel or shorter route.
middlewareDuplicated: MIDDLEWARE_DUPLICATED: names repeat in the construction tuple; assign one unique name per middleware.
middlewareMissing: MIDDLEWARE_MISSING: the operation requires an actually installed connect, abort, ping or other middleware capability.
capabilityUnsupported: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED: actual peer agreement does not support the requested runtime mode or capability.
invalidConfig: INVALID_CONFIG: factory, component, transport or transform configuration is invalid; inspect detail and correct local inputs.
probeFailed: PROBE_FAILED: a diagnostic emit/describe/redact callback failed; business execution remains isolated.
providerDuplicated: PROVIDER_DUPLICATED: provide registered a method that already has an owner; change the method or combine providers.
protocolInvalid: PROTOCOL_INVALID: codec/protocol/envelope behavior or correlated control is invalid; inspect original cause.
contractInvalid: CONTRACT_INVALID: method correlation, direction or contract identity fields violate the actual request contract.
payloadInvalid: PAYLOAD_INVALID: data, physical batch encoding or error projection violates its selected codec boundary.
providerNotFound: PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND: the receiving endpoint has no registered provider for the requested method.
providerNotSettled: PROVIDER_NOT_SETTLED: a request provider returned without an explicit success or failed result.
callbackFailed: CALLBACK_FAILED: a construction or diagnostic callback failed; native mutable errors retain type, stack and identity, foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and other values remain on cause.
internal: INTERNAL: provider threw unexpectedly; original error stays in local diagnostics while the peer receives a redacted failure.
targetUnknown: TARGET_UNKNOWN: target or receiver is unresolved, inactive or outside the original selected binding.
targetNotIdentifiable: TARGET_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: anonymous broadcast group cannot satisfy a per-instance operation.
endpointDisposed: ENDPOINT_DISPOSED: an operation used a disposed endpoint; construct a new owner instead.
cancelled: CANCELLED: actual caller AbortSignal cancelled the local send; remote effects may already have occurred.
deadlineExceeded: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the local operation deadline expired; treat this transmission attempt as failed.
contextExpired: PROVIDER_CONTEXT_EXPIRED: success or failed was called after the original provider lifetime ended; no wire effect is produced.
transport: TRANSPORT: actual physical send or terminal channel failed; preserve original transport evidence before choosing recovery. The code alone never proves nonexecution; retry requires independent evidence or idempotency/outcome reconciliation.
authenticationFailed: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: signing, verification, encryption, decryption or original replay binding failed; details stay local.
schemaInvalid: SCHEMA_INVALID: params/result parse rejected the method data; inspect normalized issues and original cause.
capabilityConflict: CAPABILITY_CONFLICT: selected middleware/features publish conflicting keys or an ambiguous runtime instance.
overloaded: OVERLOADED: execution/replay/discovery/chunk capacity refused new work; inspect its independent reason channel.
streamResultUnknown: STREAM_RESULT_UNKNOWN: transport may have sent a stream frame before rejecting; open a new stream without replaying items.
chunkInvalid: CHUNK_INVALID: physical fragment grammar is invalid; hooks observe it and the frame is not replayed.
propertyReadFailed: PROPERTY_READ_FAILED: a getter/proxy failed without a valid synchronous reporter, or that reporter threw.
idempotencyResultUnavailable: IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE: business already ran but result was not retained; resolve outcome before another attempt.
stringConversionFailed: STRING_CONVERSION_FAILED: conversion or its required synchronous reporter failed; preserve original cause.
hostTransportMissing: Exactly one genuine transport is required before opening.
hostTransportDuplicate: Multiple transports require separate hosts.
hostPluginInvalid: A copied or fabricated object lacks registered SDK identity.
hostAssemblerDuplicate: Only one member assembler can own scheduling.
hostFeatureDuplicate: A definition may be installed only once in one host.
hostPeerNameDuplicate: A same-name peer is responsive, or its one probe is already pending; reject the newcomer.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.
symbols.returns: No explicit return annotation is declared for this const.

members.name: hostTransportMissing
members.description: Host creation requires one registered transport plugin. Add a transport before retrying.

members.name: hostTransportDuplicate
members.description: Host creation received multiple transport plugins. Use one host for each transport.

members.name: hostPluginInvalid
members.description: Host creation received an object without SDK registration identity. Use the define tools.

members.name: hostAssemblerDuplicate
members.description: Host creation received multiple member assemblers. Keep one scheduling owner.

members.name: hostFeatureDuplicate
members.description: Host creation received the same feature definition more than once. Remove the duplicate * configuration.

members.name: hostPeerNameDuplicate
members.description: An incoming peer name is held by a responsive session, or another admission is probing it. * Choose a different name or close the current session.

members.name: callbackFailed
members.description: A cold Probe listener, middleware installation callback, or diagnostic reporter throws. The * original remains reachable; callers repair the callback rather than retrying side effects.

members.name: providerGenerationMismatch
members.description: The selected authenticated provider/caller generation no longer matches this task; select * again.

members.name: providerGenerationRetired
members.description: Retires an admitted forward execution with its exact generation; never replay it.

members.name: forwardLoop
members.description: A signed route already contains this Host or the selected next Host. Forwarding rejects before * admission and sending; callers must choose a route that does not revisit a Host.

members.name: forwardHopLimit
members.description: Three forwarding nodes have already been visited. Forwarding rejects a fourth before admission * and sending; callers may establish a direct connect/listen channel instead.

members.name: middlewareDuplicated
members.description: Two middleware declarations in the same factory use the same `name`. * * The installer rejects before installing any middleware. The caller gives each middleware a * unique `name`. Enforces the duplicate singleton middleware creation rule.

members.name: middlewareMissing
members.description: An operation requires a capability that is not installed. * * Examples include creating an endpoint without `connect` or calling `ping()` without `ping`. * Remote abort notification additionally needs `abort`; local signal cancellation alone does not. * The caller installs the capability required by the intended operation.

members.name: capabilityUnsupported
members.description: A Runtime API operation requires a mode or capability absent from the actual peer agreement. * Choose a supported method/mode rather than retrying the same operation.

members.name: invalidConfig
members.description: A factory, middleware, or transport descriptor or configuration field is invalid. Replay * protection also rejects encrypt-only configuration, unavailable entropy, and exhausted * counters. * * This code identifies argument and configuration failures. The caller corrects the configuration * using `detail` before retrying.

members.name: probeFailed
members.description: A probe emit, describe or redact callback fails. Probe-core reports it with the original cause * and isolates it from business execution; callers should repair or disable the diagnostic sink.

members.name: providerDuplicated
members.description: `provide()` registers the same method twice. * * A provider does not replace another provider with the same name. The caller combines the * implementations or changes the name.

members.name: protocolInvalid
members.description: A protocol codec, scheme, or envelope is invalid, the caller cannot reconstruct a response * error, or a provider receives an invalid abort payload. This is the base code for * `RpcProtocolError`. * * The caller checks that the protocol configuration matches the peer scheme. If the payload is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect, inspect the peer rather than retrying the same * message.

members.name: contractInvalid
members.description: Contract fields, direction, or request/response correlation are invalid. This is the base code * for `RpcContractError`. * * The caller checks `version`, `identifier`, sender/target direction, or `taskId`/method * correlation.

members.name: payloadInvalid
members.description: A codec payload violates its input rules, or sender-side error serialization degrades a read or * data projection. This is the base code for `RpcSerializationError`. Physical batch * shape/encoding failures preserve the contract cause; malformed semantic members are reported * individually without discarding valid siblings. * * The caller checks the data, codec, or thrown value. Do not retry the same payload if it is * already sent or cancellation has taken effect.

members.name: providerNotFound
members.description: The provider executor cannot find a provider for the target method (`Provider not found`). * * The caller checks whether `provide()` registers the method. Do not retry the failed lookup. * This is the wire code for an inbound provider lookup failure.

members.name: providerNotSettled
members.description: A non-dispatch provider does not return `ctx.success()` or `ctx.failed()`. * * The caller ensures every non-dispatch branch explicitly returns a result, or selects dispatch * if that is intended.

members.name: internal
members.description: A provider throws an unhandled exception. This is the standard code for an `INTERNAL` response. * * Only local hooks receive the redacted original exception. The peer receives `RpcRemoteError` * with code `INTERNAL`.

members.name: targetUnknown
members.description: A target or receiver is unresolved, inactive, or outside the current binding. * * The caller checks whether `targetId` is registered or discovered, or whether `receiverSelector` * returns an unknown receiver.

members.name: targetNotIdentifiable
members.description: An operation requires an individual receiver, but the target is an anonymous BroadcastChannel * group. * * The caller configures `uniqueTargetId` and `identifier` before pinning, or avoids per-instance * operations on the group.

members.name: endpointDisposed
members.description: An endpoint operation runs after disposal (`RpcLifecycleError`). * * The caller creates a new endpoint instead of reusing the closed instance.

members.name: cancelled
members.description: The caller's `AbortSignal` cancels a local send (`RpcAbortError`). * * The caller handles this cooperative cancellation separately from remote failures.

members.name: deadlineExceeded
members.description: A local deadline expires (`RpcTimeoutError`). * * The caller checks target reachability and the timeout duration. Treat the request failure as * the result of this transmission attempt.

members.name: contextExpired
members.description: `ctx.success()` or `ctx.failed()` runs after the provider task ends. * * The expired result produces no wire effects. The caller keeps response logic within the * provider's synchronous or awaited lifetime.

members.name: transport
members.description: A transport send fails, a terminal event occurs, or the transport closes (`RpcTransportError`). * * The code alone does not establish whether a send already executed. Retry only with independent * evidence that it did not execute, or use the existing idempotency/outcome reconciliation.

members.name: authenticationFailed
members.description: A per-frame authentication transform fails during encryption, signing, verification, or * decryption (`RpcAuthenticationError`). Replay protection rejects missing/invalid binding, * duplicate counters and untrusted physical sessions. * * The caller checks key and algorithm configuration. Failure details are not sent back to the * peer.

members.name: schemaInvalid
members.description: Method parameters or results violate the contract schema (`RpcSchemaValidationError`). * * The caller corrects the data using `data.issues` rather than retrying the same invalid data.

members.name: capabilityConflict
members.description: A capability is published twice, or a frozen capability registry receives another write. Also * rejects folded Feature method collisions and ambiguous runtime instances. * * The caller checks middleware for duplicate declarations of reserved capabilities. This is a * configuration error.

members.name: overloaded
members.description: A local capacity limit rejects new work in provider admission, the replay ledger, discovery * waiters, outbound IDs, or chunks. * * The caller reduces concurrency, shortens TTL, or increases capacity. This signals backpressure * rather than a logic error.

members.name: streamResultUnknown
members.description: A stream frame may have been sent before its transport rejected; the caller must open a fresh * stream and never replay delivered values.

members.name: chunkInvalid
members.description: A chunk frame has an invalid format. This is the base code for `RpcChunkError`. * * The caller checks chunk configuration (`chunkSize` ≥ 4) and the peer implementation. An invalid * frame only invokes hooks and is not retried.

members.name: propertyReadFailed
members.description: A getter or Proxy throws during `safeRead` without a synchronous reporter, or the reporter * itself throws. The caller repairs the input or supplies a synchronous `report` at a boundary * that owns a diagnostic sink.

members.name: idempotencyResultUnavailable
members.description: A keyed call already executed but its result was not retained for replay. The caller must * resolve the outcome before issuing another non-idempotent attempt.

members.name: stringConversionFailed
members.description: A string conversion throws without a synchronous reporter, or its reporter throws (cleanup ). * The caller must repair the input or provide a synchronous diagnostic sink.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Stable semantic failure codes owned by the runtime-neutral Core execution layer. The stable values below select actual contract behavior; declarations alone grant no capability.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import RpcCoreErrorCode from @migaia/rpc-host, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use RpcCoreErrorCode when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when RpcCoreErrorCode does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained const example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
providerGenerationMismatch: PROVIDER_GENERATION_MISMATCH: accepted caller/provider generation no longer matches the task; select the actual binding again.
providerGenerationRetired: PROVIDER_GENERATION_RETIRED: an admitted forwarded execution retired with its exact generation; never replay it.
forwardLoop: FORWARD_LOOP: signed route revisits this or the selected next Host; choose another route.
forwardHopLimit: FORWARD_HOP_LIMIT: three forwarding nodes were already visited; use a direct channel or shorter route.
middlewareDuplicated: MIDDLEWARE_DUPLICATED: names repeat in the construction tuple; assign one unique name per middleware.
middlewareMissing: MIDDLEWARE_MISSING: the operation requires an actually installed connect, abort, ping or other middleware capability.
capabilityUnsupported: CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED: actual peer agreement does not support the requested runtime mode or capability.
invalidConfig: INVALID_CONFIG: factory, component, transport or transform configuration is invalid; inspect detail and correct local inputs.
probeFailed: PROBE_FAILED: a diagnostic emit/describe/redact callback failed; business execution remains isolated.
providerDuplicated: PROVIDER_DUPLICATED: provide registered a method that already has an owner; change the method or combine providers.
protocolInvalid: PROTOCOL_INVALID: codec/protocol/envelope behavior or correlated control is invalid; inspect original cause.
contractInvalid: CONTRACT_INVALID: method correlation, direction or contract identity fields violate the actual request contract.
payloadInvalid: PAYLOAD_INVALID: data, physical batch encoding or error projection violates its selected codec boundary.
providerNotFound: PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND: the receiving endpoint has no registered provider for the requested method.
providerNotSettled: PROVIDER_NOT_SETTLED: a request provider returned without an explicit success or failed result.
callbackFailed: CALLBACK_FAILED: a construction or diagnostic callback failed; native mutable errors retain type, stack and identity, foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and other values remain on cause.
internal: INTERNAL: provider threw unexpectedly; original error stays in local diagnostics while the peer receives a redacted failure.
targetUnknown: TARGET_UNKNOWN: target or receiver is unresolved, inactive or outside the original selected binding.
targetNotIdentifiable: TARGET_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE: anonymous broadcast group cannot satisfy a per-instance operation.
endpointDisposed: ENDPOINT_DISPOSED: an operation used a disposed endpoint; construct a new owner instead.

deadlineExceeded: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED: the local operation deadline expired; treat this transmission attempt as failed.
contextExpired: PROVIDER_CONTEXT_EXPIRED: success or failed was called after the original provider lifetime ended; no wire effect is produced.
transport: TRANSPORT: actual physical send or terminal channel failed; preserve original transport evidence before choosing recovery. The code alone never proves nonexecution; retry requires independent evidence or idempotency/outcome reconciliation.
authenticationFailed: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED: signing, verification, encryption, decryption or original replay binding failed; details stay local.
schemaInvalid: SCHEMA_INVALID: params/result parse rejected the method data; inspect normalized issues and original cause.
capabilityConflict: CAPABILITY_CONFLICT: selected middleware/features publish conflicting keys or an ambiguous runtime instance.
overloaded: OVERLOADED: execution/replay/discovery/chunk capacity refused new work; inspect its independent reason channel.
streamResultUnknown: STREAM_RESULT_UNKNOWN: transport may have sent a stream frame before rejecting; open a new stream without replaying items.
chunkInvalid: CHUNK_INVALID: physical fragment grammar is invalid; hooks observe it and the frame is not replayed.
propertyReadFailed: PROPERTY_READ_FAILED: a getter/proxy failed without a valid synchronous reporter, or that reporter threw.
idempotencyResultUnavailable: IDEMPOTENCY_RESULT_UNAVAILABLE: business already ran but result was not retained; resolve outcome before another attempt.
stringConversionFailed: STRING_CONVERSION_FAILED: conversion or its required synchronous reporter failed; preserve original cause.
hostTransportMissing: Exactly one genuine transport is required before opening.
hostTransportDuplicate: Multiple transports require separate hosts.
hostPluginInvalid: A copied or fabricated object lacks registered SDK identity.
hostAssemblerDuplicate: Only one member assembler can own scheduling.
hostFeatureDuplicate: A definition may be installed only once in one host.
hostPeerNameDuplicate: A same-name peer is responsive, or its one probe is already pending; reject the newcomer.

symbols.name: authFeature
symbols.signature: export declare const authFeature: (config: IRpcAuthenticationConfig) => IRpcFeaturePlugin;
symbols.purpose: Configure original signing/verification and optional paired encryption without changing replay or error ownership.
symbols.core:
Actual feature object; retain it and install at most once per host.
encrypt: Outbound sync/async encryption runs after the endpoint wraps its encoded value with replay metadata and before signing. Throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with its cause.
encrypt.value: Replay-bound authentication envelope produced by the endpoint, including its encoded payload; not the bare application payload.
encrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Encrypted value or its Promise, passed unchanged into sign.
Leave encrypt and decrypt out together when messages need signatures but not encryption. In that case, sign receives the unencrypted authentication envelope: the message data together with the information used to detect replay. Omitting encryption does not remove signing or verification.
Configure `encrypt` with `decrypt` for confidentiality and `sign` with `verify` for integrity; `encodedType` names the actual protected representation.
decrypt: Inbound sync/async decryption runs on the value recovered by verify. The endpoint then validates the recovered authentication envelope and replay binding.
decrypt.value: Verified protected value returned by verify.
decrypt.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Recovered replay-bound authentication envelope or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED with the original cause.
Omit decrypt only when encrypt is also omitted. After verify checks the signature and recovers the inner value, the endpoint directly checks that value as the authentication envelope, including its replay information. It does not try to decrypt the value.
sign: Outbound sync/async signing runs after optional encryption and returns the complete protected frame representation. Signing and verification are required even without encryption.
sign.value: Encrypted value when encrypt exists, otherwise the replay-bound authentication envelope.
sign.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Signed representation or its Promise; throw/rejection normally becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED. Keep the declared encodedType output domain.
There is no default signing function. Provide sign together with verify whenever authentication is enabled. This remains required when encrypt and decrypt are configured: encryption alone is insufficient, and omitting sign rejects the configuration.
verify: Inbound sync/async verification receives the protected frame and must recover its authenticated inner value; returning a boolean is not a verification verdict protocol.
verify.value: Protected value received at the authentication pipeline edge.
verify.context: IRpcAuthenticationContext issued by the endpoint: direction is outbound/inbound, endpointId is its local identifier and platform is its configured IRpcPlatformValue.
Authenticated inner value or its Promise, passed to decrypt when configured; reject or throw on invalid signatures. Local reporting retains the original verification failure, which may be sensitive; the peer receives a sanitized summary. Other returned values still undergo envelope/replay validation.
There is no default verification function. Provide verify together with sign so incoming protected messages can be checked and their inner values recovered. If sign is supplied without verify, construction rejects the configuration before the endpoint becomes active.
encodedType: Declared protected-output domain must match the next physical pipeline edge. Encrypt/decrypt and sign/verify are complete pairs, at least signing is required, and encryption additionally requires signing.
any: do not impose a declared protected-output value category.
Leave the declared output domain unconstrained; transforms may still change representation.
Declare that the protected output is text for the subsequent pipeline edge.
Declare that the protected output is a byte array for the subsequent pipeline edge.
Configure original signing/verification and optional paired encryption without changing replay or error ownership.

port: Original native port created by the application MessageChannel, Worker launcher or actual runtime resource.

send: Sends one actual carrier value; completion means the physical boundary completed, not that a remote provider executed.
send.message: Original complete message value accepted by this actual carrier domain.
send.options: Optional IRpcSendOptions supplies original physical transfer references.
Void or Promise<void> from the physical owner; native message-port and Worker send failures retain native Error/DOMException type and stack. Mutable unclassified errors gain Core TRANSPORT in place; foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and immutable values remain on cause.
subscribe: Subscribes to actual inbound messages; the original native registration is detached when its last logical listener leaves.
subscribe.listener: Application callback receives a record containing data and optional actual peerId/origin/source; return void. Adapter-owned listener errors use onListenerError.

close: Retires this transport according to actual ownership; owned resources may be closed, borrowed resources retain their caller-owned native lifetime.

symbols.signature: export declare function createMessageListenerHub<TMessage>(): IMessageListenerHub<TMessage>;
symbols.purpose: Creates a local listener fan-out hub sharing one physical attachment across distinct callback identities.
symbols.core:
Local hub with size, has(listener), add(listener, attach), remove(listener, detach), dispatch(message, invoke) and clear(detach). add/remove/clear return void except remove returning whether a member was removed; has returns boolean. Dispatch snapshots membership and propagates invoke failures. Attach/detach callbacks are synchronous; failure leaves the logical change uncommitted.

`size`: Current number of distinct registered callback identities.

`has`: Checks whether this exact callback is registered. `listener`: Original application callback passed to add. True only for a currently registered callback identity.

`add`: Attaches the physical listener before adding the first callback; duplicate callbacks remain one Set member. `listener`: Application callback to retain by identity. `attach`: Synchronous physical registration callback; a throw leaves this callback unregistered. No result; first successful attachment and membership are retained.

`remove`: Detaches before removing the last callback; a detach throw keeps membership so release can be retried. `listener`: Exact original callback supplied to add. `detach`: Synchronous physical removal callback invoked only for the last member. True if removed, false if absent; detach failure propagates.

`dispatch`: Snapshots callbacks before invocation; reentrant membership changes affect subsequent dispatches, and an invoke throw stops this dispatch. `message`: Actual message received from the physical carrier. `invoke`: Synchronous dispatcher receiving each snapshot listener and the message; use observeListener to isolate failures. No result; invokes each snapshot member unless the dispatcher throws.

`clear`: Detaches the physical listener before clearing all callbacks; failure keeps membership intact. `detach`: Synchronous physical removal callback. No result; membership is empty after successful return.

symbols.name: createRuntimeByteConnection
symbols.signature: export declare function createRuntimeByteConnection(channel: IRuntimeByteIO, options: IRuntimeByteOptions, diagnostics: IRuntimeByteDiagnostics): Promise<IRuntimeByteConnection>;
symbols.purpose: Perform original framed control negotiation over real ordered byte I/O and retain its accepted connection.
symbols.core:
channel: Actual IRuntimeByteIO owned by the physical adapter.
options: Initiator/responder offer, verifier, deadline and original connection policy.
diagnostics: Adapter-owned canonical error/code/text data.
Promise of negotiated IRuntimeByteConnection; its original close releases connection cleanup before physical close. It creates no host endpoint.
role: Choose initiator to send hello, or responder to verify the received offer before accepting the ordered byte channel.
auth: Responder authentication policy: required invokes the original verifier; none admits without a token verifier.
auth.mode: Use required for authenticated responder admission, or none for the explicitly unauthenticated responder path.
auth.verify: Receives the remote authentication value and peer info; returns an optional principal synchronously or asynchronously. Throwing or rejection refuses the handshake.
offer: Local capability and protocol proposal supplied by this adapter; only the received acknowledgement establishes the accepted agreement.
platform: Adapter-issued carrier label used in diagnostics; this presentation value grants no peer identity or trust.
expectedStringText: Canonical adapter diagnostic used when the physical connection supplies a non-text frame to its text pipeline.
peerId: Direct peer address issued by the held deployment; runtime negotiation retains its own actual peer identity.
signal: Optional caller-owned abort signal stops opening and handshake work through the existing resource owner.
handshakeTimeoutMs: Finite nonnegative opening budget in milliseconds; omission retains the canonical 10000 ms deadline.
scheduler: Borrowed monotonic clock and timers for this preparation; optional connection schedulers default to systemScheduler.
report: Synchronous original background and secondary-cleanup error observer; it receives the original error without changing the business result.
ipc: Original connection labels, bounded data/control backlog and diagnostic observer; no second message queue is created.
ipc.connectionId: Stable local connection label issued by the adapter for backlog diagnostics.
ipc.sessionId: Session label issued by the actual accepted connection for diagnostic correlation.
ipc.maxPendingData: Positive safe-integer data capacity including active sends; omission keeps 256 entries.
ipc.maxPendingControl: Positive safe-integer reserved control capacity including active sends; omission keeps 8 entries.
ipc.log: Receives original backlog and physical diagnostic records; observer failures do not replace business settlement.
parameters: channel: IRuntimeByteIO
options: IRuntimeByteOptions
diagnostics: IRuntimeByteDiagnostics
symbols.returns: Promise<IRuntimeByteConnection>
overloadSignatures: export declare function createRuntimeByteConnection(channel: IRuntimeByteIO, options: IRuntimeByteOptions, diagnostics: IRuntimeByteDiagnostics): Promise<IRuntimeByteConnection>;

symbols.name: createRuntimeProviderGovernor
symbols.signature: export declare function createRuntimeProviderGovernor(channel: IRemoteChannel, options: IRuntimeProviderPolicy, closeSession: () => Promise<void>, report: (error: unknown) => void): IRuntimeProviderGovernor;
symbols.purpose: Enforce original connection rate, payload and idle limits at actual provider execution.
symbols.core:
channel: Actual accepted remote channel.
options: Original IRuntimeProviderPolicy chosen by the native owner.
closeSession: Callback closing only this native session on the original policy.
report: Observer for original background/cleanup diagnostics.
Governor with original limit/provider/stream wrappers and close. It owns its connection timers/subscriptions, not another endpoint.
maxCallsPerMinute: Per-connection admitted-call rate limit maintained by the original provider governor.
maxPayloadBytes: Maximum payload size admitted by this connection before its provider executes.
maxConsecutiveTimeouts: Consecutive deadline failures tolerated by the existing connection governor before session retirement.
idleTimeoutMs: Idle connection budget in milliseconds; the original governor owns the timer and closes only this session.
violationLimit: Number of quota violations handled by the existing governor before closing this connection.
overflow: Adapter-owned source, code and message for quota rejection; diagnostics never grant control authority.
parameters: channel: IRemoteChannel
options: IRuntimeProviderPolicy
closeSession: () => Promise<void>
report: (error: unknown) => void

export declare const IpcLogEventName: { /** Accepted backlog crossed the high watermark. */ readonly 'ipc.backlog.high': 'ipc.backlog.high'; /** Backlog drained below the low watermark. */ readonly 'ipc.backlog.low': 'ipc.backlog.low'; /** The selected lane could not admit another envelope. */ readonly 'ipc.backlog.rejected': 'ipc.backlog.rejected'; /** An admitted physical send failed. */ readonly 'ipc.send.failed': 'ipc.send.failed'; /** Explicit stderr text supplied by a process owner. */ readonly 'ipc.stderr': 'ipc.stderr'; };

symbols.purpose: Connection-local diagnostic event names distinguish capacity transitions, send failures and explicit process stderr.
symbols.core:
ipc.backlog.high: Accepted capacity reached or exceeded ceil(capacity * 0.75), after previously being below its high watermark.
ipc.backlog.low: After a high event, accepted capacity drained to or below floor(capacity * 0.5).
ipc.backlog.rejected: The corresponding whole-envelope lane refused capacity.
ipc.send.failed: The original physical send or diagnostic dispatch failed.
ipc.stderr: An explicit process standard-error record is supplied locally.

symbols.name: IRpcTransport
symbols.signature: export type IRpcTransport<Message = unknown, Transfer = unknown> = { /** Send one selected frame; rejection reports physical failure, not whether the peer executed it. */ send(message: Message, options?: IRpcSendOptions<Transfer>): void | Promise<void>; /** Attach a receive listener and return the operation that detaches that registration. */ subscribe(listener: (message: IRpcInboundMessage<Message>) => void): () => void; /** Retire adapter-owned I/O; Core calls this on disposal unless ownership is borrowed. */ close?(): void | Promise<void>; /** Observe physical failures so Core can settle affected pending operations. */ onTransportError?(listener: (error: unknown) => void): () => void; /** Observe failures from delivery/observation listeners without treating them as peer replies. */ onListenerError?(listener: (error: unknown) => void): () => void; /** Optional carrier observation capability; the contract layer never calls this slot. */ observe?(probe: IRpcCarrierProbe): () => void; /** Known direct peer identity; omission leaves selection to connect/discovery policy. */ readonly peerId?: string; /** Expected native origin used by the built-in connection verifier. */ readonly origin?: string; /** Stable carrier label for verification policy and diagnostics. */ readonly platform: IRpcPlatformValue; /** Describes whether adapter messages share one peer, many peers, or a broadcast group. */ readonly topology?: IRpcTransportTopologyValue; /** Declared frame representation; omission leaves the adapter representation unrestricted. */ readonly encodedType?: IRpcTransportEncoding; /** Borrowed skips physical close; owned or omitted delegates close to endpoint cleanup. */ readonly ownership?: IRpcTransportOwnership; /** Adapter-owned source proof for multiplexed transports. */ readonly sourceProof?: (source: unknown, origin?: string) => boolean; /** True only when the adapter can prove that no further messages can be delivered. */ readonly closed?: boolean; };
symbols.purpose: Original adapter-owned carrier interface; its operations, source proof and cleanup stay separate from Core protocol ownership.
symbols.core:
send: Sends one actual carrier value; completion means the physical boundary completed, not that a remote provider executed.
send.message: Original complete message value accepted by this actual carrier domain.
send.options: Optional IRpcSendOptions supplies original physical transfer references.
Void or Promise<void> from the physical owner; native message-port and Worker send failures retain native Error/DOMException type and stack. Mutable unclassified errors gain Core TRANSPORT in place; foreign semantic identities stay unchanged, and immutable values remain on cause.
subscribe: Subscribes to actual inbound messages; the original native registration is detached when its last logical listener leaves.
subscribe.listener: Application callback receives a record containing data and optional actual peerId/origin/source; return void. Adapter-owned listener errors use onListenerError.
Idempotent removal of this registration; native cleanup failure may throw and preserve retry ownership.
close: Retires this transport according to actual ownership; owned resources may be closed, borrowed resources retain their caller-owned native lifetime.
Void or Promise<void>; actual native cleanup failures remain observable. Consult the adapter-specific close policy.
onTransportError: Subscribes to original physical/read/terminal failures without treating them as application provider results.
onTransportError.listener: Application callback receives original unknown error, returns void; secondary failure is retained by the adapter reporter boundary.
Removal releases this failure observer only.
onListenerError: Subscribes to original message-listener or physical-observer callback failures independently of transport failure.
onListenerError.listener: Application callback receives original listener error and returns void; its own failure is collected by the original adapter.
Removal releases this diagnostic observer and may surface collected reporter failures.
observe: Installs original physical observation; replacing it retires the preceding observation generation without acquiring lifecycle ownership.
observe.probe: Actual IRpcCarrierProbe port supplied by the installed endpoint emitter.
Disposer retires only this observation generation, including when the same probe was later reinstalled.
peerId: Optional original peer identity attributed by the actual adapter; caller labels do not grant verified identity.
origin: Optional actual origin attributed by the adapter, not a caller assertion of trust.
platform: Actual carrier platform label for presentation and diagnostics.
topology: Actual peer topology supplied by the adapter.
encodedType: Actual accepted carrier encoding domain.
ownership: Actual original physical ownership determining cleanup responsibility.
sourceProof: Optional original adapter callback receives native source and optional origin, synchronously returns boolean; labels alone cannot replace this proof.
closed: True only when this adapter can prove no future message delivery; logical detach alone is insufficient.

timeoutMs: Finite nonnegative milliseconds, or false to disable the inherited deadline for this call.

idempotencyKey: Application-issued key identifying the same logical operation across retries; use the original key for reconciliation.
Omitted: automatic keys are generated only for declared idempotent requests.
orderKey: Application-selected lane key grouping calls for provider-wide ordered admission in the runtime profile.
Omitted: no ordered lane is requested.
cancel: Cancellation intent evaluated by the final provider start boundary.
Omitted: no before-start cancellation intent.
Permit cancellation before the provider starts the invocation.
transfer: Caller-owned ArrayBuffers transferred through a carrier that actually supports native transfer.
Omitted: no explicit native ownership transfer.

symbols.purpose: Detail of one connection, returned by `get(target)`, listed by `list()` and in `describe().connections`.
symbols.core:
methods: Method paths callable on the other side, from its accepted directory.
counters: Call counters: `inFlight` (calls not yet finished) is measured; `sent`, `received`, `errors`, `lastActiveAt` are reported unavailable; or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
recent: Recent lifecycle records (`IRuntimeRecent`), newest last.
identity: Identity `{ name, instanceId }` the other side announced, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
generation: Generation accepted from the other side (not the local restart count).
kind: How the connection was configured: `spawn`, `connect` or `listen`.
direction: Who started it: `spawned`, `spawned-by` (this side is the child), `connect` or `listen`.
carrier: Name of the physical carrier, such as a MessagePort or stdio.
connection: `{ status }`: `ready`, `closed`, `departed`, or unavailable.
unit: Supervised unit `{ kind, state, generation, degraded }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
health: Health check metric `{ state, failures }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
restartCount: Number of restarts as a metric, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
resources: Sampled resources (pid or threadId, memory, CPU time, event-loop utilisation), or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.
lastExit: Last exit `{ generation, reason, code, signal, error? }`, or `{ status: "unavailable", reason }` when the owner cannot observe it.

symbols.purpose: One accepted logical Peer exposing local identity, calls, passive events and deterministic connection cleanup.
symbols.core:
self: Frozen local peer name and instanceId minted or supplied during this connection construction; it is not a remote authentication principal.
outcome: Queries the original remote operation ledger for a prior idempotency key, without dispatching that operation again.
outcome.idempotencyKey: The caller-issued key supplied as options.idempotencyKey on an earlier request to this connection.
Promise of IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult; support and availability come from the accepted remote runtime contract.
describe: Queries the local accepted peer detail asynchronously. Without format returns IRuntimeDetail; json, yaml or toml returns the admitted text projection. It does not claim unavailable physical metrics.
describe.options: Optional query format from IRuntimeQueryOptions; omitted returns the object snapshot.
Promise of local detail or formatted text, following the selected query format.
on: Registers a future RuntimeEventName listener after construction; factory resolution already represents initial readiness. Listener return is ignored and failures are contained by the runtime reporter.
on.event: A RuntimeEventName value such as ready or exit; it selects future connection lifecycle notifications.
on.listener: Callback receives IRuntimeEvent from this connection; return is ignored and throws or rejected thenables are reported.
Idempotent removal function for this registration; closing the peer clears its publisher.
close: Ends this logical connection and releases its owned channel resources; platform factories also terminate a worker or child they spawned.
Shared completion Promise retaining the original close operation identity; no new calls are admitted once closing begins.
[Symbol.asyncDispose]: Scoped asynchronous cleanup is the exact original close operation, including its Promise identity.
The same completion Promise as close(), including platform-owned resource cleanup.
request: Calls a method the other side provides and waits for its result. Default deadline 30000 ms (`defaultTimeoutMs`); errors keep their native type and `(source, code)`.
request.method: Dotted path from the accepted remote provide directory.
request.payload: Single application payload accepted by that method; omit for a parameterless method.
request.options: Local controls from IRuntimeCallOptions, separate from the payload.
The method result, typed from `TRemote`.
notify: Sends a one-way call; no result comes back.
notify.method: Dotted path from the accepted remote provide directory.
notify.payload: Single application payload accepted by that method; omit for a parameterless method.
notify.options: Local controls from IRuntimeCallOptions, separate from the payload.
Resolves once the call was sent.
stream: Calls a method that returns an iterable and yields its items as they arrive.
stream.method: Dotted path from the accepted remote provide directory.
stream.payload: Single application payload accepted by that method; omit for a parameterless method.
stream.options: Local controls from IRuntimeCallOptions, separate from the payload.
An async iterator of the yielded items.
group: Sends several calls as one batch and returns the outcome of each step in order.
group.steps: Steps `{ method, payload? }` in order.
group.options: Batch options such as `timeoutMs` and `signal`.
One outcome per step (success value or error).

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import IRuntimePeer from @migaia/rpc-host/plugin, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use IRuntimePeer when its type contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when IRuntimePeer does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained type example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
self: Frozen local peer name and instanceId minted or supplied during this connection construction; it is not a remote authentication principal.
outcome: Queries the original remote operation ledger for a prior idempotency key, without dispatching that operation again.
outcome.idempotencyKey: The caller-issued key supplied as options.idempotencyKey on an earlier request to this connection.
Promise of IRpcRuntimeOutcomeResult; support and availability come from the accepted remote runtime contract.
describe: Queries the local accepted peer detail asynchronously. Without format returns IRuntimeDetail; json, yaml or toml returns the admitted text projection. It does not claim unavailable physical metrics.
describe.options: Optional query format from IRuntimeQueryOptions; omitted returns the object snapshot.
Promise of local detail or formatted text, following the selected query format.
on: Registers a future RuntimeEventName listener after construction; factory resolution already represents initial readiness. Listener return is ignored and failures are contained by the runtime reporter.
on.event: A RuntimeEventName value such as ready or exit; it selects future connection lifecycle notifications.
on.listener: Callback receives IRuntimeEvent from this connection; return is ignored and throws or rejected thenables are reported.
Idempotent removal function for this registration; closing the peer clears its publisher.
close: Ends this logical connection and releases its owned channel resources; platform factories also terminate a worker or child they spawned.
Shared completion Promise retaining the original close operation identity; no new calls are admitted once closing begins.
[Symbol.asyncDispose]: Scoped asynchronous cleanup is the exact original close operation, including its Promise identity.
The same completion Promise as close(), including platform-owned resource cleanup.
request: Calls a method the other side provides and waits for its result. Default deadline 30000 ms (`defaultTimeoutMs`); errors keep their native type and `(source, code)`.
request.method: Dotted path from the accepted remote provide directory.
request.payload: Single application payload accepted by that method; omit for a parameterless method.
request.options: Local controls from IRuntimeCallOptions, separate from the payload.
The method result, typed from `TRemote`.
notify: Sends a one-way call; no result comes back.
notify.method: Dotted path from the accepted remote provide directory.
notify.payload: Single application payload accepted by that method; omit for a parameterless method.
notify.options: Local controls from IRuntimeCallOptions, separate from the payload.
Resolves once the call was sent.
stream: Calls a method that returns an iterable and yields its items as they arrive.
stream.method: Dotted path from the accepted remote provide directory.
stream.payload: Single application payload accepted by that method; omit for a parameterless method.
stream.options: Local controls from IRuntimeCallOptions, separate from the payload.
An async iterator of the yielded items.
group: Sends several calls as one batch and returns the outcome of each step in order.
group.steps: Steps `{ method, payload? }` in order.
group.options: Batch options such as `timeoutMs` and `signal`.
One outcome per step (success value or error).

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content: Use a negotiated platform channel without introducing another proxy lifecycle.
